investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-17T02:20–02:27Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent never reached a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner collected zero evidence, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so they are ineligible regardless of capacity. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free a slot (no lower-priority victims found), every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never receives a running VM, so it cannot populate vmIdPresent or remoteState, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259 is fully unmet.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no allocatable capacity for new pods — directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

The 4 remaining nodes lack the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource label or the node affinity/selector required by remote-agent pods, meaning they are structurally ineligible and cannot absorb overflow even if they have free CPU/memory.
A surge in concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from users or other eval runs) may have saturated the 2 kata-capable nodes before this eval run began, leaving no room for the probe pod.

A node running kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads may have recently become unavailable (e.g., cordoned, drained, or failed), reducing the effective pool from a larger number to 2 nodes and exhausting capacity faster.

The cluster's kata peer-pods quota or the underlying VM provider quota (e.g., cloud instance limits for the peer-pod VM type) may have been reached, preventing the kata device plugin from advertising additional slots.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-17T02:20–02:27Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent never reached a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner collected zero evidence, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, so they are ineligible regardless of capacity. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free a slot (no lower-priority victims found), every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1885) never receives a running VM, so it cannot populate vmIdPresent or remoteState, and the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256–259 is fully unmet.
